gap: No result ChatGPT got states the AeroClip 2's actual certified speech-quality score: G-MOS 3.55 in standard mode, the figure behind the Guinness open-ear clip-on record. On the same G-MOS scale, Guinness lists 3.68 for Anker's own in-ear Liberty 5 Pro.
standout_why: I opened soundcore.com's AeroClip 2 page (results 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 11 are that page and its variants). It names the Guinness title and the 2026-08-31 date but gives no score. Our own dealectric.com comparison says only 'G-MOS certified'. HearWiki says its figures are not lab measurements and come from maker data. SoundGuys' C50i product page lists only spec-sheet figures, with no measured results and no review. I fetched TechRadar's AeroClip 2 review twice and got only the headline both times. None of the pages I could read gives a G-MOS number, a timed battery run, or a measured latency or leakage figure for either product.
decides: This confirms the pick and doesn't change it. The AeroClip 2's call advantage now has a number (3.55 G-MOS, standard mode) instead of just 'Guinness-certified'. It sits 0.13 below the 3.68 that Guinness lists for Anker's in-ear Liberty 5 Pro, so it is a strong score for an open-ear clip-on. I could not find any measured call score for the C50i, so the page can't show a head-to-head figure. The call gap remains the maker's 6-mic-versus-2-mic claim plus the AeroClip 2's certified score. On battery, named reviewers' runs (about 7–8 h for the AeroClip 2 and about 7 h for the C50i) put the two closer together than the 8 h vs 7 h spec suggests. That supports buying the C50i unless calls matter.
